content_metadata.description: The image illustrates seed germination in a bean plant, showcasing stages from a dormant seed to a young plant.

activities.description: Display two bean seeds with intact seed coats.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Illustrates the initial stage of seed germination.
scenes.title: Dormant Seed

videoEditingDetails.description: Zooming in on the seeds for clarity.

activities.description: Show the radicle breaking through the seed coat and growing downward.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Shows the first visible sign of germination.

narrativeProgression.description: Radicle emergence signals the start of growth.

scenes.title: Radicle Emergence

videoEditingDetails.description: Display animation of the radicle's growth.

activities.description: The hypocotyl elongates, pushing the cotyledons above the ground.

narrativeProgression.description: The plant begins to reach upwards.

videoEditingDetails.description: Highlight the upward growth of the hypocotyl.

mood.description: Vital stage of nourishment and growth.

activities.description: Epicotyl emerges, giving rise to the first foliage leaves.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Marks the transition to a more complex plant.
scenes.title: Epicotyl Development

videoEditingDetails.description: Emphasize the emergence of true leaves.

activities.description: A mature seedling with foliage leaves and a well-developed root system.

mood.description: Achievement of a full cycle from seed to plant.

videoEditingDetails.description: Show full growth with leaves and roots.

climax.description: Emergence of the first true leaves.

storylines.description: The progression from seed dormancy to a functioning young plant, showing key stages and growth.

content_metadata.title: Seed Germination Process in a Bean Plant

trimmingSuggestions.description: Development of epicotyl and true leaves.

The resumption of active growth of the embryo resulting in rupture of a seed coat and emergence
of a young plant is called as germination.
There are three stages of germination.
One is pre germination.
Second is germination and third one is post germination.
In case of pre germination, first the high rehydration takes place that is imbibeation
of water.
RNA and protein synthesis is stimulated.
Increased metabolism that is increased respiration takes place.
Later the hydrolysis of reserve food material by the enzymes will be done.
Then change in cell ultra structure will be seen.
Then induction of cell division and cell growth will be seen.
And in case of germination, the rupture of seed coat, emergence of seedling usually radical
will be the first.
Then post germination, controlled growth of root and shoot axis and then controlled transport
of material from food stores to growing axis is seen.
Then sentences are aging, sentences of the food storage tissues will be seen.
There are three phases of seed germination.
One is imbibeation phase.
Second is latent phase and exponential phase growth.
In case of imbibeation phase, water is absorbed by the seed which activate the gibbalic acid
synthesis.
This increased gibbalic acid synthesis will internally to increase in DNA synthesis which
led to the RNA synthesis or transcription which finally led to the production of amylase
enzymes or other hormones or other enzymes also.
Which this amylase enzyme will degrade the starch, convert into sugar, this sugar enter
inside the epicortile which led to the growth and germination of the seed.
Lament phase is further divided into phase 1, 2 and 3.
In phase 1, rapid uptake of water takes place and the onset of mRNA synthesis will start.
Then the onset of starch degradation takes place.
Then glycolysis and fermentation of starch hydrolysis which led to the cell wall biosynthesis
non-functional protein degradation, mitochondrial assembly and amino acid biosynthesis.
Then in phase 2, that is TCA cycle where in phase 2, coliaptyl emerges emergency.

There are two types of germination.
One is hypogeal germination and another one is epigel germination.
In case of hypogeal germination, the cotillidane is present inside the ground level after germination
of the seed.
